;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**[[Amnesty International]] says it has conducted a report which says that [[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw|armed forces]] "have killed civilians, including children in indiscriminate air attacks" in [[Rakhine State|Rakhine]] and [[Chin State|Chin]] states, urging the [[United Nations Security Council]] to launch a [[war crime]]s investigation. Myanmar has been fighting the [[separatist]] [[Arakan Army (Kachin State)|Arakan Army]] in the region. The [[government of Myanmar|government]] did not immediately respond to calls for comment. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/myanmar-air-raids-killed-children-amount-war-crimes-200707194910335.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**At least 180 bodies have been found in [[mass grave]]s in [[Djibo]], [[Burkina Faso]], where [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldiers]] are fighting [[jihadist]]s. It is suspected that the [[government of Burkina Faso|government]] forces were involved in mass [[extrajudicial execution]]s. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53333366 (BBC News)]
*[[July 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**A [[suicide bomb]]er kills three people when he drives a military vehicle packed with [[explosive]]s near the provincial governor's residence in [[Kandahar]], [[Afghanistan]]. The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks/taliban-suicide-bomber-kills-three-as-violence-rises-despite-peace-push-idUSKBN2491SP (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Local [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] leader Sheikh Wazeem Bari and two members of his family are shot dead in [[Bandipore district]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. Senior [[Ministry of Home Affairs (India)|Ministry of Home Affairs]] official [[K. Vijay Kumar]] blames the Islamic terrorist group [[Jaish-e-Mohammed]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/bjp-leader-his-father-and-brother-shot-dead-in-kashmir-cops-arrest-his-security-guards/story-UsqR5iWYycDNLGmNGOBwiP.html (''Hindustan Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on airlines]]
**[[Delta Air Lines]] ends service to 11 airports in an effort to reduce domestic flights by 80% and international flights by 90% due to aviation restrictions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.businessinsider.com/delta-will-stop-flying-to-11-us-cities-list-2020-6 (''Business Insider'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*One person is killed and four others injured when a 20-metre [[Crane (machine)|crane]] collapses at a building site where flats were being constructed in the [[Bow, London|Bow]] district of [[East London]], [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-crane/one-dead-and-four-injured-in-london-crane-collapse-idUSKBN2492TG?il=0 (Reuters)]
*American actress [[Naya Rivera]] is declared missing at [[Lake Piru]] in the [[Los Padres National Forest]] of [[Ventura County, California]], after she reportedly rented a boat and swam in the lake with her four-year-old son. Rivera's son was found on the boat unharmed, while the [[Ventura County Sheriff's Office]] have initiated a [[search and rescue]] operation for the actress. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-people-naya-rivera/glee-actress-naya-rivera-missing-at-california-lake-authorities-say-idUSKBN24A0PW (Reuters)]

****The [[United States]] surpasses three million cases of COVID-19 and sets a daily record of 62,021 new cases. ***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]

;International relations
*[[Mexico–United States relations]], [[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] hosts a meeting at the [[White House]] with [[President of Mexico|Mexican President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] to discuss the new [[United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]]. [[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] declines to attend. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2020/07/08/trump-mexico-amlo-visit/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Lithuania–Russia relations]]
**[[Lithuania]] bans [[Russia]]n state-owned television network [[RT (TV network)|RT]] due to its connection with [[Dmitry Kiselyov]], who is sanctioned by the [[European Union]] for his role in the 2014 [[Ukrainian crisis]]. [https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1195727/lithuania-bans-kremlin-s-rt (LRT)]

;Law and crime
*[[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act#Legal challenges|Affordable Care Act legal challenges]], [[Contraceptive mandate]]
**In a 7–2 decision on ''[[Little Sisters of the Poor Saints Peter and Paul Home v. Pennsylvania]]'', the [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]] upholds regulations that allow employers with religious or moral objections to decline to provide contraception coverage under the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act|Affordable Care Act]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/08/us/supreme-court-birth-control-obamacare.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/courts_law/supreme-court-obamacare-birth-control-mandate/2020/07/08/0b38a352-c123-11ea-b4f6-cb39cd8940fb_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States]] rules in favor of the [[Little Sisters of the Poor]]. The victory at the court comes after nine years of their legal fight against the [[Barack Obama|Obama]]-era “contraception mandate”. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/we-are-overjoyed-little-sisters-of-the-poor-react-to-scotus-decision-42155 (Catholic News Agency)]
*Former [[Governor of Chihuahua]] and wanted fugitive [[César Duarte Jáquez]] is arrested by police in [[Miami]], [[Florida]], after being in hiding since 2017. He is wanted on corruption charges in [[Mexico]], after allegedly misappropriating public funds. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-mexico-crime-governor/fugitive-former-mexican-governor-arrested-in-miami-idUKKBN24939U?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Ivory Coast]]
**Ivory Coast's [[Prime Minister of Ivory Coast|Prime Minister]] and [[2020 Ivorian presidential election|candidate for the presidential election]] [[Amadou Gon Coulibaly]] dies in office after falling ill at a ministerial meeting. He had recently returned from [[France]] after undergoing treatment for heart problems. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53340236 (BBC News)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on association football]]
**[[Major League Soccer]] resumes its [[2020 Major League Soccer season|2020 season]] after a four-month hiatus caused by the COVID-19 pandemic with a month-long [[MLS is Back Tournament|tournament]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]], [[Florida]]. [[2020 FC Dallas season|FC Dallas]] will sit out the tournament after 10 players and a coach were diagnosed with COVID-19. [https://www.foxnews.com/sports/mls-to-resume-season-minus-1-team-amid-growing-virus-concern (Fox News)]
